tasks.title: adapters and payments: a refund is recorded as Stripe reports it (pending, succeeded, failed, canceled), never as done on a 200
tasks.goal: `PaymentsAdapter::create_refund` returns only the `re_…` ID (`app/adapters/src/payments.rs`), so `refunds::finish` treats any answer as `Refunded`, sets the row `succeeded` and appends the ledger `refund` entry, and `reconcile::own_refund` counts any answer as refunded, even when Stripe answered `pending`, `requires_action`, `failed` or `canceled` (external audit A03, D-1753; D-1545 (2) already recorded the ledger side). (1) The typed refund is additive for production callers (this task is a `harness` task because four DONE tasks' test fakes gain one trait impl each): `app/payments/src/refund_stripe.rs` defines a payments-owned trait `RefundStripe: PaymentsAdapter` (the `IntentStripe` and `ReconcileStripe` pattern) with `refund(idempotency, payment_intent) -> Refund` and `fetch_refund(id) -> Refund`, where `Refund { id, state, amount_cents, currency, payment_intent }` and `RefundState::{Pending, RequiresAction, Succeeded, Failed, Canceled}`; an unknown state string is an error, never a success, and the refund must name the PaymentIntent asked for. It is implemented for `StripeHttp` there, over two new inherent HTTP calls on `StripeHttp` in `app/adapters/src/payments.rs` (the `PaymentsAdapter` trait and its `create_refund` stay unchanged until T132 retires `create_refund`). `refunds::finish`, the retry and `reconcile::own_refund` take `&impl RefundStripe`, and so do the public functions that reach them: `request_refund`, `run_refund_retry` and `early_fraud_warning` (`app/payments/src/refunds.rs:78`–`:135`), `reconcile` and `run_reconcile` (`app/payments/src/reconcile.rs:125`, `:424`) and T064's `run_late_refund` (`app/payments/src/late.rs:112`). The fakes in `tests/integration/tests/disputes.rs`, `late_success.rs`, `reconcile.rs` and `ledger_1000_jobs.rs` each gain one `impl RefundStripe` whose `refund` answers `Succeeded` with the ID their `create_refund` already returns and whose `fetch_refund` answers the same; nothing else in those files changes (no blanket impl over `PaymentsAdapter`, which would conflict with the `StripeHttp` impl). tasks.title: portals: every homeowner Verify code is bound to its purpose by a local challenge with a try cap
tasks.goal: Pentest PT-03 and the PT-02 gap beyond the report (D-2348; SEC-055, SEC-008, PRIV-031). One Twilio Verify service serves every purpose and `VerifyAdapter::check_code(to, code)` (`app/adapters/src/verify.rs:50`, :86) is not bound to one, so `confirm_request` (`app/portals/src/data_download.rs:210`) acts on any of her open requests (up to 30 days old) after any passing code for her phone, the sign-in code included, and homeowner sign-in (`finish_sign_in`, `app/portals/src/homeowner_portal.rs:164`) keeps no local challenge; neither has an app-side try cap. Build: (1) `migrations/0176_portals_code_challenge.sql` adds `portals.code_challenge` (ID, purpose `homeowner_signin`, `data_copy` or `data_delete`, subject ID (her contact for sign-in, the request for copy and delete), sent at, used at, tries; app role SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE of `tries` and `used_at` only). (2) `app/portals/src/code_challenge.rs`: the rule (SEC-055): a challenge lives as long as the Verify code (10 minutes from its first send, the `SEND_WINDOW_SECONDS` both files use); a send (`send_sign_in_code`, `open_request` and a new `resend_request_code` for an open request) made while an unused challenge of that purpose and subject is still alive reuses it and does not reset its tries or its send time, because Twilio keeps one pending code per number for its life, so the cap is truly 5 per code; a send after the newest challenge expired or was used opens a new one; each is written in a short committed transaction before Verify is called. A check is refused before Verify is called unless the newest unused, unexpired challenge of that purpose and subject exists; it reserves a try against that challenge by one atomic `UPDATE ... SET tries = tries + 1 WHERE id = $1 AND used_at IS NULL AND tries < CODE_TRIES RETURNING`, committed before the Verify call (the cap is `business_auth::CODE_TRIES`, the same constant as T272; a reservation never comes back, so a crash or a timeout uses a try); a right code then uses the challenge with a conditional `UPDATE ... SET used_at = $2 WHERE id = $1 AND used_at IS NULL` in the same transaction as the action it confirms (the session start, or the confirmed audit row with the copy or the delete), and when no row changes (a second right check got there first) the action rolls back and nothing is done twice. No pooled connection, transaction or reservation is held across the Verify await (pentest PT-04's availability side, D-2349): `send_sign_in_code`, `finish_sign_in`, `open_request`, `confirm_request` and `resend_request_code` take `&PgPool` in place of `&mut PgConnection` and acquire a connection only for each short database step, releasing it before Verify is called; T307 calls them with the router's pool. Picks' codes and business sign-in keep their own rows (T272 binds the business code to its sent challenge). (3) No change to `stand_ins/twilio.py`: it keys a verification by `to` only, which is the shared-service model these tests need. Tests in `tests/security/tests/code_purpose.rs` (TD-SEC-60): a code sent for one purpose is refused for another before Verify is called (a sign-in code cannot confirm a delete whose own challenge expired or was used; a pick code cannot sign in); 20 simultaneous wrong checks reach Verify at most 5 times and the sixth is refused; a used challenge is refused; a right code and the action commit together; a re-send inside the code's life reuses the challenge and gives no more tries, and one after expiry or use opens a new one; two simultaneous right checks act once; with a fake Verify that hangs, 30 concurrent sends and checks leave a pool of 5 connections able to serve another request (the matrix's AVAIL-01). Update the `portals` `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md` section 10 and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: harness: the authorization matrix gets public, owner and action-link doors and an HTTP probe for every served realm route
tasks.goal: Matrix doors before the serving tasks (D-2440; SEC-019, SEC-048, SEC-034, SEC-004 to SEC-008, SEC-026; D-1945, D-736, D-2429). T088's authorization matrix (`tests/security/tests/auth_matrix.rs`) gives every route of the generated route table a door and panics on a path it does not name (`:107`), and `td_sec_01_route_table_is_generated_and_every_path_has_a_door` fails on any served `/h` or `/b` route (`:527` to `:531`), because those realms are probed only through the guard function "since those routes are not served yet". Before any of them, extend the matrix; nothing in it is exempted, loosened or removed. (1) New doors in `door`, beside the existing ones: `Public` for `/healthz`, `/help` and every path below it, the legal pages (`/terms`, `/privacy`, `/sms-terms`, `/your-data`, `/business-data`) and any route the `site` module serves (the route table records the module of each `.route(` call; a site route outside this list is still public); `ActionLink` for `/b/a/` paths (T148's signed email action links, before the `/b` business arm); `Owner` for `/owner` and every path below it except the sign-in paths, which stay `SignIn`. `allowed`: `Public` admits every actor; `ActionLink` admits no session by itself (the link is the key); `Owner` admits only the owner. (2) `td_sec_01_route_table_is_generated_and_every_path_has_a_door` no longer fails on a served realm route; instead every served path of the `Homeowner`, `Business`, `Owner`, `ActionLink` and `Public` doors must have a row in `docs/architecture.md` section 13 reading `yes` (which `app/server/tests/route_wiring.rs` already proves served), so the HTTP probe below reaches it; a served one without that row fails naming it. With nothing served under those doors today the check passes. (3) `app/server/tests/door_matrix.rs` (new; a test crate may not depend on `askhava-server`, D-736, so the HTTP probe lives in the server crate): against `server::build_router` over a real test database, the same six actors as the matrix (anonymous, homeowners A and B, businesses X and Y, the owner, signed in the way `auth_matrix.rs` signs them in) send every method of every section 13 row reading `yes` whose path falls under those five doors (the same prefix rules, restated in the file): a `Homeowner` route admits A and B only, to their own records (A's page never names B's job or token), and gives anyone else a 4xx with a link to `/h/sign-in` and no detail; a `Business` route admits X and Y only, a `{pick}` or `{complaint}` of the other business is the one not-found answer, and anyone else gets a 4xx with a link to `/b/sign-in` and no homeowner detail; an `Owner` route admits only the owner and gives anyone else a 4xx with a link to `/owner/sign-in`; an `ActionLink` route opens only for the token minted for that kind, object and member (`portals::api` minting, as T148's tests do), a `GET` changes nothing (SEC-026), and a token for another kind, object or member, or none, is the one not-found answer; a `Public` route answers every actor's `GET` without a session and its body holds none of the fixtures' names, phones, addresses, tokens or job numbers. tasks.title: calls: a PIN draw fails only when the OS source fails, and one failed draw costs one draw
tasks.goal: Moved out of T311, which the runner claimed before this fix reached main (D-2451). PIN draws that fail for no reason (D-2451; CALL-003, CALL-017, D-1755): `os_number` (`app/calls/src/pins.rs:53`) rejects two-byte values of 60,000 or more and gives up after 4 tries, so about 1 call in 19,600 it returns `None` although the OS source works (8.4% rejection, 0.0845⁴ ≈ 5.1e-5), and `draw_pin` (`:46`) uses `map_while`, so that one `None` ends all 8 draws; `allocate_pin` then gives none, `assign_number` (`app/calls/src/service.rs:137`) calls `refuse_line` (`:162`), which raises a false High `calls.pool_exhausted` alert and refuses the line with `NoFreePin` (the masked-line assignments at `app/picks/src/release.rs:236` and `app/picks/src/settle.rs:148`; T254's one `picks.line_retry` hides most of them). Fix: `os_number` returns `None` only when the OS source fails, by drawing again until a value below the largest multiple of 10,000 the width holds, with a cap so large it is never the reason (for example 64 two-byte draws, about 2e-69), the bytes coming from an injectable fill function so the rejection step can be tested; `draw_pin` uses `filter_map`, so a failed draw costs one of the 8 draws, not all of them. Unit tests beside the existing ones in `pins.rs`: a source that fails once and then gives a free PIN succeeds; an injected byte source that gives values of 60,000 or more several times and then one below gives that value modulo 10,000; an injected source that fails gives `None`. The two existing unit tests and TD-CALL-13's 500-line integration test (`tests/integration/tests/call_pins.rs`) pass unchanged. After T311 (the other owner of `pins.rs`, whose read-back changes this task must keep). Update the `calls` `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: privacy and server: the scrubber remembers names across a homeowner's texts and knows her vault name
tasks.goal: The served SMS route scrubs each text with `vault_name: None` and a fresh `NameMemory` (`read` in `app/server/src/inbound_text.rs`), so a name she stated in an earlier text, and her name in the vault, are not removed from a later one (AI-003, AI-020; external audit A02, D-1752). Build the privacy-owned, contact-aware read. (1) `migrations/0130_privacy_stated_names.sql`: `privacy.stated_name` (contact ID with a foreign key to the vault contact `ON DELETE CASCADE`, the name sealed like a vault field with its key version, created time; unique per contact and blind-indexed value so a repeat is one row); the app role gets SELECT, INSERT and DELETE only. (2) `app/privacy/src/scrub_context.rs`: `privacy::api::read_inbound_for(conn, vault, contact, raw, words)` opens the contact's vault name under the existing `(Messaging, Inbound)` grant and her stated names, scrubs with both (`Known::vault_name` and `NameMemory::mark_known` per stored name), stores any name the scrub newly marks as stated, and returns only the `Inbound` (flags and `ScrubbedText`): no plaintext leaves `privacy`. Because no plaintext leaves, this read may run inside the delivery's transaction (D-1752 narrows D-752's in-transaction refusal to functions that return plaintext); its audit rows commit or roll back with the delivery and a resent delivery is read and audited again. SEC-047's hourly rate check stays on for this read: it is counted under the `(Messaging, Inbound)` grant's own action, once per text, against its 14-day baseline with D-750's floor of one read an hour, so the alarm tracks inbound text volume (a flood of texts is a signal Casey should see); no exclusion and no new threshold, tested with a steady hour (no alert) and a burst over three times the baseline (one alert). (3) The route resolves the sender (blind index only) before reading, then calls `read_inbound_for`; a business sender's text is scrubbed with an empty context as now. (4) Purge and rotation: the PRIV-007 purge and "Delete my data" (`app/privacy/src/purge.rs`, T092's) delete her stated names with her name; `rotate_batch` in `app/privacy/src/vault.rs` re-seals them under the new key. No raw name, message history or digest of a name goes to any intake row, log, task payload or alert. Update `docs/architecture.md` section 8, the `privacy` and `server` `CLAUDE.md` files and `docs/decisions.md`.

(2) `raise_alert` (`app/ops/src/service.rs:96`) inserts with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and returns the open alert's ID when one exists (no new row, so no new push); a raise after it was resolved opens a new one. Read every caller of `raise_alert` (about 60): those that need one alert per event (each HELP request, each dispute, each failed purge) already carry a distinct subject; list in the decision any caller whose behaviour changes. Tests in `tests/integration/tests/alert_dedupe.rs` (TD-OPS-34): two raises of one kind and subject leave one open row and return its ID; after it is resolved a raise opens a new one; two subject-less raises of one kind leave one; two concurrent raises leave one. A persona library (`wargames/personas.py`) holds both sides: ordinary, confused and vanishing homeowners; Spanish speakers; tenants; STOP and START mid-job; pranksters and AI-credit drainers (photo spam, bursts of requests, endless rambling intake, re-entry loops, opt-out and opt-in churn, one- and two-word messages); people posing as businesses; contractors gaming quotes (bounced contact details, edits, double picks, after-hours claims, never confirming). Chaos injectors (`wargames/chaos.py`): duplicate and replayed webhooks, out-of-order texts, the clock at the 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. quiet-hour edges and at the 24-hour and 4-business-hour timer edges (local lane), a vendor outage mid-flow and the AI returning junk (local lane, through the stand-ins' fault and plant headers). tasks.title: AI-call budgets per conversation and per job, and no AI call before the area check
tasks.goal: Credit-drain defense for the war games (D-1154): AI-021's global daily cap stays, and below it AI-028's per-step budgets apply: no AI call before the consent text and the area check; 2 readings per inbound message, 1 reword per bank question (at most 8), 1 follow-up, card and project file 1 each plus 1 per EDIT (at most 3), 4 concept prompts, 2 screening calls a photo for at most 3 photos; backstops of 40 calls per conversation per Arizona day and 60 per job, with the card call always reserved so no budget lands on it; a verified web-chat session shares its phone's budget and an unverified one makes no call; quote reads 3 per business per job, outside the job's budget; only the first 1,600 characters of a scrubbed message are sent, while the AI-off card keeps her full scrubbed words. Past a budget the step runs on the AI-off path (INT-021) with nothing said and an `ai.call_stat` row with outcome `budget`; `models::calls_today` (`app/ai/src/models.rs`) excludes `budget` rows as it excludes `daily_cap` rows, so refused calls never use up the AI-021 cap. `IntakeCall` carries the conversation, job, step and (for quote reads) business it is for; the caller in `intake` passes them; the budgets are settings in `AiConfig`; the migration adds the `budget` outcome and the conversation, job, step and business columns to `ai.call_stat`. The global daily cap (AI-021, D-811) becomes an atomic admission: before the provider call, one statement reserves a slot for this Arizona day (a counter row per day updated with `... WHERE used < cap RETURNING`, or an equivalent single-statement reservation) on its own short transaction, so concurrent calls past the cap never reach the transport; a retry of one logical call uses its reservation, an abandoned or timed-out reservation still counts for that day, and the `ai.daily_cap` alert is raised once a day under the same race (D-1757). No database connection or open transaction is held across an AI provider await (AI-029, D-2038): the entry the app calls takes the pool, reads the AI-008 switch and makes the admission and the budget reservations each on its own short connection and releases it, awaits the provider (up to AI-023's timeout, retries and backoff included) with no connection held, then takes a connection again to record the call. With no connection held, every AI-028 budget check is a single-statement reservation like the AI-021 admission (only while the budget has room), so concurrent readings of one message (a duplicate or replayed webhook) cannot pass its 2-reading limit, the 1-reword limit or the per-day and per-job backstops together; a refused reservation makes no call and records outcome `budget`. Intake has no caller that applies a reading yet (`app/intake/src/question_bank.rs` calls only `accept_question`), so this task builds the first one in `app/intake/src/service.rs`: it reads one inbound message through the gated `read_intake` and applies the reading only if the step is still current on the new connection, which means the conversation has no inbound message and no `intake.intake_answer` row newer than the message the call was made for; otherwise the reading is recorded and discarded. Calling that function from the text and web-chat paths is T299's (IC-23, D-2065); the AI writing calls are IC-53's (no owner yet). `app/ai/src/switch.rs` (the gated `read_intake`) is this task's for that change. Other tasks' tests call `read_intake` with a `&mut PgConnection` (`app/ai/src/tests/adapter_calls.rs`, `tests/integration/tests/ai_zero_retention.rs`, `tests/integration/tests/prop_prompt_injection.rs`) and are not this task's to change: keep that form compiling for them as a thin wrapper that no app code calls. AI-029's other half, the inbound-text webhook committing before any AI call, is T299's, which wires the AI reading into the text path (IC-23, D-2065); that path makes no AI call yet.

tasks.title: calls and server: a random stored PIN per line, unique on its number, durable PIN-try counts, and the inbound voice route
tasks.goal: A line's PIN is its ID modulo 10,000 (`calls::api::job_pin`, D-1684), and line IDs are not secret; the 6-a-day count is the caller's input with no storage (D-1685); and no inbound-voice route serves the TwiML (D-1708). D-1684 and D-1685 named T078 or T080, both DONE without it (external audit A09, D-1755). (1) `migrations/0151_calls_pins_attempts.sql`: a `pin` column on `calls.number_pool` (four digits, drawn from the OS random source, unique among open lines of one pool number by a partial unique index) and `calls.pin_try` (a digest of the calling number, never the number: HMAC-SHA-256 under the ID secret with the domain label `pin-try|v1` over the normalized E.164 number, derived with `core`'s ID-secret derivation as `IdempotencyKey::derive` is, listed under `ID_SECRET` in the PRIV-024 key inventory and re-derived when that secret rotates; pool number; Arizona day; count; queries in `app/calls/src/models.rs`), app role SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE of the count only. (2) `app/calls/src/pins.rs`: allocation in `assign_number`'s transaction (`app/calls/src/service.rs`) retries a collision a bounded number of times, then raises the existing pool alert and refuses the line; `job_pin` and every read of the PIN come from the stored column (`routing.rs`), never the line ID; the try count is one atomic `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... RETURNING` per wrong try, so concurrent wrong tries cannot pass 6 a day, and a repeated Twilio callback (same CallSid and digits) is not another try (recorded per CallSid). (3) `app/server/src/inbound_voice.rs`: the signature-checked Twilio voice webhook (SEC-016) for the pool numbers, recorded by CallSid (SEC-017), finding the party, lines, stored counts and STIR/SHAKEN attestation and serving `calls::api` TwiML (prompt, PIN, read-back on A attestation only, dial), merged in the shared `lib.rs`; the same migration creates `calls.call_start` (the parent CallSid unique, the line, the start time, the dialed leg's SID filled later by T271; app role SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE of the dialed SID only), and the webhook stores the call's start there, once per parent CallSid, at the moment it answers with the dial, so FEE-022 judges each call by when it started (D-1836). No line ID reaches a homeowner or business. Update `docs/architecture.md` section 10, the `calls` and `server` `CLAUDE.md` files and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: payments and picks: the fee fixed at the pick is stored by payments, a press must match it, and a fee-mode switch after the pick is refused before any charge
tasks.goal: No code stores the fee fixed at the pick: `picks`' `new_pick` (`app/picks/src/service.rs:340`) says "No fee ... here", `payments`' `fee_at_pick` (`app/payments/src/rules.rs:496`) is a pure function nothing outside tests calls, and `open_intent` and `confirm_and_pay` (`app/payments/src/charge.rs:91`, `:146`) charge whatever `Press::amount_cents` the caller passes (`app/payments/src/models.rs:325`), checking only that it is not 0 (third external audit, D-1871). And the fee-mode check runs only after Stripe has charged: `record_fee_at_confirm` (`app/payments/src/service.rs:344`) refuses with `ConfirmError::Mismatch` when the mode changed, so a switch between the pick and Confirm leaves money moved with no ledger entry until the reconcile; and nothing stores the fee terms in force: `switch_fee_mode` (`app/payments/src/service.rs:207`) only returns them and every caller passes its own `FeeTerms`. (1) `migrations/0155_payments_fee_terms_pick_fee.sql`: `payments.fee_terms`, one row (mode and authorization version), seeded with `tiers` and `AUTHORIZATION_VERSION`, the app role SELECT and UPDATE only; and `payments.pick_fee` (`pick_id` primary key, `business_id`, `job_id`, `mode` `tiers` or `flat`, `kind` `charged` or `fee_free`, `amount_cents` at or above 0 and above 0 only for `charged`, `terms_version`, `fixed_at`), the app role SELECT and INSERT only. `switch_fee_mode` writes the new terms to `payments.fee_terms` in its own transaction with its audit row (T108's owner switch calls it and stores nothing else), and `payments::api::fee_terms_in_force(conn)` reads them; `picks` and T261 read the terms only through it. (2) `app/payments/src/pick_fee.rs`: `payments::api::fix_fee_at_pick(tx, pick, business, job, &PickedFee, at)` writes it once (a repeat with the same values is a no-op, different values an error) and `pick_fee(conn, pick)` reads it. (3) `new_pick` computes the fee with `fee_at_pick` from the chosen quote (its amounts and period), the job's category and job type facts and `fee_terms_in_force`, through the modules' `api`s (FEE-005's inputs only, D-1415), and calls `fix_fee_at_pick` in the pick's own transaction; a pick whose fee can't be fixed is not stored. (4) `open_intent` and `confirm_and_pay` read `pick_fee` before anything else: no row, a different business or job, a $0 fee, or `amount_cents` other than the stored one is the new `ChargeError::FeeMismatch`, and Stripe is not called; an existing `pick_intent` whose amount differs from the stored fee is the same refusal. (5) The mode check moves before the charge: `may_confirm` takes the pick, reads `fee_terms_in_force` itself and refuses with the new `ConfirmError::FeeModeChanged` when the stored `mode` differs from them, before any PaymentIntent is opened or confirmed; `record_fee_at_confirm` takes the pick and writes the stored fee, comparing the gate's `Authorized` (whose mode matched the pick's at the gate) with the stored mode, so a switch that commits after the gate changes nothing for this pick and the post-charge write can no longer fail for a mode switch. D-072 still applies to every pick made after a switch. Tests in `tests/integration/tests/fee_fixed_at_pick.rs`. This is a harness task because it changes tests of DONE tasks (T060's `fee_mode_switch.rs` and `fee_at_pick.rs`, T062's `charge_attempts.rs`, T189's `confirm_and_pay.rs`) and T263's `fee_limit_race.rs`: each fixture only gains the stored fee terms and the stored pick fee its presses now need (and `may_confirm` the pick), and no expected value changes. Update the `payments` and `picks` `CLAUDE.md` files and `docs/decisions.md` (`docs/architecture.md` section 3 already lists the new table, D-1871).

tasks.title: architecture test: dynamic SQL in a migration is a TD-SEC-10 finding unless allow-listed with a reason
tasks.goal: Dynamic SQL hides schema references from TD-SEC-10 (D-1677): `schema_refs` in `tests/integration/tests/architecture_migrations.rs` lexes dollar-quoted bodies as SQL but cannot see a schema name built while a migration runs, so a migration such as `DO $x$ BEGIN EXECUTE format('ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA %I REVOKE ...', nsp); END $x$;` names no schema literally and passes (seen in T250's third attempt, PR #293, not merged). In that test (T226's, then T250's, taken over here after T250 merges) add a dynamic-SQL rule over each migration's lexed tokens (the tokens `schema_refs` reads, so comments and `'...'` strings never count). A file gives one finding, `migrations/<file>: dynamic SQL (`<construct>`) hides schema references from this check`, naming the first construct found, when it holds: a `DO` statement (the token `do` first in a statement, at the start of the file or after `;`, so `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and a rule's `DO INSTEAD` never count); an `execute` token not followed by `function`, `procedure`, `on` or `,` (the PL/pgSQL dynamic statement, including inside a `CREATE FUNCTION` or `CREATE PROCEDURE` body, `RETURN QUERY EXECUTE` and a cursor's `FOR EXECUTE`; a trigger's `EXECUTE FUNCTION` and `GRANT`/`REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION` are not dynamic); or a call of `format`, `quote_ident`, `quote_literal` or `quote_nullable` (the name followed by `(`). The SQL of each query macro and `query_file*` file under `app/` gets the same finding for `DO` and `execute` (a `format(` there only formats a value). A file is exempt only when its path is in a new constant `DYNAMIC_SQL_ALLOWED: [(&str, &str); N]` (path, one-line reason); it starts with one entry, `migrations/0019_core_db_migrations.sql`, whose `DO $guard$` block only raises an error when the role `askhava_app` is missing and builds no SQL (T012). An entry whose file is missing or no longer holds dynamic SQL is itself one finding, so the list cannot go stale. The checks take the allow list as a parameter: `td_sec_10_migrations_and_sql_obey_the_rules` passes the constant and each plant passes its own, so a planted path never enters the real list. Planted cases giving exactly one finding each: a `DO` block, an `EXECUTE` in a `CREATE FUNCTION ... LANGUAGE plpgsql` body, a `format()`-built statement, a query macro holding `EXECUTE`, and a stale allow-list entry; planted cases giving none: an allow-listed file holding a `DO` block, an `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, a `CREATE TRIGGER ... EXECUTE FUNCTION` and a `GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION`. Every earlier case, T250's included, still gives exactly its one finding: each T250 case whose plant holds a `DO` block (those proving a `DO` block voids the REVOKE exception, such as a REVOKE beside a `DO` block and a REVOKE inside one) runs with its planted file on its own allow list, so it still proves only its own rule. If another migration on `main` holds dynamic SQL when this task starts, list it only when it builds no schema name at run time, with its reason; otherwise stop and report. Update the test's `//!` header to name the rule, and the `migrations/` entry of `docs/architecture.md` section 2 (T226's paragraph on this test) to name it too (section 4 rule 3 already states it, D-1677).

tasks.title: portals: the sign-in link cap and the code-try cap are atomic admissions, so concurrent requests cannot pass them
tasks.goal: D-1725 allows at most 5 sign-in links per member in 15 minutes and D-1777 at most 5 failed code checks per link, but both are check-then-act: `send_one` counts links (`models::links_since`, `app/portals/src/models.rs`) and then inserts and sends, and `check_once` counts `auth_failed` events, calls Verify and records the failure afterwards (`app/portals/src/business_auth.rs:444`, `:652`), so simultaneous requests that all see 4 all go through (second external audit B01, D-1837). (1) Links: the count and the insert of the new `portals.login_link` row happen in one short transaction under a per-member transaction-scoped lock (`pg_advisory_xact_lock` on the member's ID under a `portals` key namespace), committed before the email is sent; no transaction is held across the mail call. (2) Code tries: `migrations/0167_portals_code_tries.sql` adds `portals.code_try` (link ID, try number 1 to 5 unique per link, reserved time, outcome `pending`, `right`, `wrong` or `abandoned`; app role SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE of the outcome only); a check first reserves the next try number in its own short transaction (the unique key and the check constraint refuse a sixth), then calls Verify with no transaction open, then records the outcome; a reservation left `pending` (a crash or a Verify timeout) counts as a used try, so a restart never gives a try back; the fifth used try uses the link up and shows the "stopped working" screen as today; a right code consumes the link once (the existing guarded `UPDATE`), and a concurrent right code and wrong code never both sign in. Each wrong or failed check still writes its `auth_failed` security event (SEC-048). T089's per-IP and per-business limits sit in front of these and never re-count links or tries (D-1837). Tests in `tests/security/tests/signin_admission.rs` with 20 simultaneous requests over several pooled connections. Update the `portals` `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md` section 10 and `docs/decisions.md`. Pentest PT-04 and PT-03's business half (D-2349): `send_once` (`app/portals/src/business_auth.rs:630`) holds a transaction across `codes.verify.send`, and `check_once` (:664) never requires that a code was sent for its link. This sets aside only D-1776's held transaction. (3) The same migration adds `portals.code_send` (link ID primary key, reserved at, outcome `pending`, `sent` or `failed`); a press reserves the link's one send in a short committed transaction (a new row, or a `failed` one, or a `pending` one older than the adapter's 15-second timeout plus a minute, which a crash left), calls Verify with no transaction open, then records `sent` or `failed`, so a failed send can be pressed again and two presses at once send once; it replaces the `code-sent:<link>` marker row. (4) `check_once` refuses a link whose send is not `sent` before any try is reserved or Verify is called. Tests in `signin_admission.rs` (TD-SEC-38): a failed send can be retried; 20 simultaneous presses send once; a check with no sent code reaches Verify zero times; with a fake Verify that hangs, no transaction is open during the wait. (5) No pooled connection is held across a Verify call either (PT-04's availability side, D-2349): `device_step`, `send_once` and `check_once` take the handler's `&PgPool` (`state.pool`, already in this file) in place of `&mut PgConnection` and acquire a connection only for each short database step, releasing it before the send or the check; with a fake Verify that hangs, 30 concurrent presses and checks leave a pool of 5 connections able to serve another request (the matrix's AVAIL-01, TD-SEC-38).

tasks.title: adapters and stand-ins: local write-once storage that a racing writer cannot alter, object delete and list, and the Twilio message-body delete
tasks.goal: (1) B05 (second external audit, D-1841): `write_once` (`app/adapters/src/storage.rs:72`) writes every attempt to the same deterministic `<name>.<key>.part` with `std::fs::write`, which truncates and rewrites one shared file, then hard-links it into place, so a racing retry can empty or change an object already published. Each attempt now creates its own temporary file exclusively (`create_new`, a random suffix from the OS source), writes it fully, `sync_all`s and closes it, and publishes with `hard_link` (which never replaces an existing object); it compares bytes with an existing object only once that object's publication is complete, and removes only its own temporary file. (2) D-1803's missing capabilities, additive so no existing fake changes (the `RefundStripe` pattern, D-1753): `StorageDelete: StorageAdapter` with `delete_object(name)` (an absent object is success) and `list_objects(prefix)`, implemented for `LocalStorage`; `SmsBodyDelete: SmsAdapter` with `delete_message_body(sid)` for Twilio's documented message delete (or body redaction, whichever the vendor documents for removing a body; the choice recorded), implemented for `TwilioSms` in `app/adapters/src/sms.rs`. tasks.title: server: every request has a whole-request time limit, answered 503 with the security headers
tasks.goal: `tower-http`'s `timeout` feature is enabled (`Cargo.toml:38`) but `build_router` (`app/server/src/lib.rs:75`) applies no time limit, so a request whose body trickles in, or a handler that hangs, holds its connection and task without end (third external audit, D-1870; threat model D13). (1) `app/server/src/request_timeout.rs`: the limit is a setting, `ASKHAVA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS`, added to the typed settings in the shared `app/core/src/settings.rs` (D-493) and read from them at start-up (default 60 seconds, allowed 10 to 300; any other value, or one that is not a whole number, stops start-up with a message naming the key, never the value). 60 seconds is longer than the longest chain of bounded vendor calls one handler makes today (a Confirm press makes at most three Stripe calls at the adapters' 15-second limit, `app/adapters/src/base.rs:211`), so the limit stops only a stalled request, never a slow vendor call the adapters already bound. (2) `build_router` takes the limit and applies it to every route, inside the `security_headers` layer, so a timed-out request is answered `503 Service Unavailable` with `Retry-After: 5`, the SEC-012 headers and `Cache-Control: no-store`, and its handler future is dropped (every write a handler makes is in a transaction or keyed, so a dropped request commits nothing half-done; a webhook sender retries a 503, SEC-017). A Confirm press dropped in the middle of a Stripe call leaves its attempt `sent`; it is never retried until Stripe, asked directly, says it failed (FEE-037's sent-then-fetch path in `confirm_and_pay` and `repeat_press`), so the limit can never cause a second charge. The worker has no HTTP routes and is unchanged. (3) `app/server/tests/request_timeout.rs`, with `tokio::time::pause`: a route that never answers is cut at the limit with 503, `Retry-After`, the security headers and the request ID; a route that answers just inside it is untouched; a body that stops arriving is cut the same way; each bad setting value stops start-up. Update the `server` `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md` section 2 (the layer order) and `docs/decisions.md`. (4) Fourth external audit F6 and F37 (D-2208): `build_router` also applies `tower-http`'s `CatchPanicLayer` (the `catch-panic` feature is on, `Cargo.toml:38`) inside the security-headers layer, so a handler that panics is answered 500 with the SEC-012 headers, `no-store` and the request ID and a body that names no panic message; and `ASKHAVA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` with a path after its host (anything but the trailing slash it drops, `app/core/src/settings.rs:397`, the shared typed settings) stops start-up naming the key, since the routes are served at the root and the Twilio signature check signs the public base plus the route path. Tests in `app/server/tests/server_hardening.rs` (TD-SEC-55, TD-SEC-56).

Add rows to `docs/catalog/worked_examples.yaml` after W40 (W41 onward): for each recurring period (weekly, every two weeks, monthly, quarterly, yearly) and each edge ($500.00 and $1,500.00), the one-cent-wide range (low L, high L + $0.01) whose exact 4-month basis is the nearest reachable on each side of the edge (the highest basis below it and the lowest at or above it), plus, where a one-cent-wide range reaches it exactly, the basis a cent above the edge. Worked from `four_months` (`app/payments/src/rules.rs:290`) on `main`: only yearly reaches a cent below, at and a cent above both edges ($1,499.97–$1,499.98 → $499.99, $1,500.00–$1,500.01 → $500.00, $1,500.03–$1,500.04 → $500.01; $4,499.97–$4,499.98, $4,500.00–$4,500.01 and $4,500.03–$4,500.04 for $1,500); quarterly reaches a cent below and at but not a cent above ($374.99–$375.00 → $499.99, $375.00–$375.01 → $500.00; $1,124.99–$1,125.00 and $1,125.00–$1,125.01 for $1,500); weekly, every two weeks and monthly reach none of the three exactly, so their rows are the nearest on each side (weekly $28.84–$28.85 → $499.98 and $28.85–$28.86 → $500.15, $86.53–$86.54 → $1,499.94 and $86.54–$86.55 → $1,500.11; every two weeks $57.68–$57.69 → $499.93 and $57.69–$57.70 → $500.02, $173.07–$173.08 → $1,499.98 and $173.08–$173.09 → $1,500.07; monthly $124.99–$125.00 → $499.98 and $125.00–$125.01 → $500.02, $374.99–$375.00 → $1,499.98 and $375.00–$375.01 → $1,500.02); 22 rows in all, numbered W41 to W62 in this order: weekly, every two weeks, monthly, quarterly, yearly, each period's $500 rows then its $1,500 rows in rising basis (W41–W44 weekly, W45–W48 every two weeks, W49–W52 monthly, W53–W56 quarterly, W57–W62 yearly); the four whose basis is above $1,500 are W44 (weekly, $1,500.11), W48 (every two weeks, $1,500.07), W52 (monthly, $1,500.02) and W62 (yearly, $1,500.01), each $75 under the cap and $199 without it; each row's `fee_basis` and `fee` are worked from D-033 (exact sum of the ends times the period's monthly factor times 4, divided once, rounded down to the cent), with the recurring cap of $75 applying above $1,500 (FEE-039). tasks.title: calls and server: a voice read-back confirm connects only the line that was read back
tasks.goal: Fourth external audit F39 (D-2201; CALL-005, CALL-002): after two bad PINs from a business's linked phone the read-back names the homeowner of one line (`calls::routing` answers `Answer::ReadBack(line, words)`, `app/calls/src/routing.rs:406`), but `pins::reply` drops the line (`app/calls/src/pins.rs:299`), the voice route's confirm URL carries only the try number (`app/server/src/inbound_voice.rs:206`), and `voice_confirm` connects whichever open line of the caller's business is newest at the press (`pins.rs:335`), so a line opened, closed or moved between the read-back and the press bridges the caller to a homeowner who was never read back. (1) The line read back is bound to its try: `migrations/0174_calls_readback_line.sql` adds a nullable `readback_line` (the line's ID) to the try's `calls.pin_call` row, inserted with the row: `Step::ReadBack(line)` is known in `judged_count` before `count_once` writes the row, so the line goes in that insert, in that transaction, and no `UPDATE` grant is added. Twilio's resend of the read-back turn returns early in `judged_count` (the row exists) and today `answer_for` recomputes from the live pool; the repeat reads back the bound line from the row instead, never a newly chosen one; the confirm URL stays `?confirm=<try>`, so nothing about the line goes to Twilio or the caller. (2) `voice_confirm` reads the bound line and connects it only when the press confirms, the try is the recorded A-attested read-back try (as today), and that line is still open on the call's pool number and still belongs to the caller's linked business; otherwise it answers as for an unconfirmed press today (ask for the PIN again, or hang up) and never connects another line; the newest-line lookup is removed. (3) Tests in `app/server/tests/voice_confirm_line.rs` through the served voice route with signed fake requests (TD-CALL-17): a second line B opened for the same business between the read-back and the press connects A and never B; the read-back line A closed while B is open, or A no longer the caller's business, connects nobody; a confirm on a try other than the read-back try (a row with no `readback_line`) connects nobody; a resend of the read-back turn reads back the bound line; the unchanged case connects exactly the line read back, and a repeated identical confirm connects it again and writes no second `call_start`. Every existing `app/server/tests/inbound_voice.rs` and `tests/integration/tests/call_pins.rs` case passes unchanged. The overseer runs an independent security review of the hand-in (D-2201). tasks.goal: Fourth external audit F44 (D-2204; FEE-027, FEE-050): `payments::mark_auto_submit` (`app/payments/src/disputes.rs:169`) commits the `auto_submit` mark and only then queues the submit task, and `record_owner_submission` (`:197`) commits `submitted_at` and only then appends the $15 countering fee, each on whatever connection its caller passes; a failure between the two leaves the mark or `submitted_at` set, every retry answers `false`, and the submit task or the fee is lost for good. tasks.title: payments: the nightly reconcile catches up after an outage from its last good run, reads Stripe in pages, and checks refund amounts
tasks.goal: Sixth audit U-07 and U-05's reconcile half (D-2304, D-2303; FEE-029, FEE-051, FEE-028). After T288 (which keeps unsettled charges open) and T333: (1) `LOOKBACK` is 7 days (`app/payments/src/reconcile.rs:57`), so a charge whose events all fell before a reconcile outage of more than 7 days is never read. `migrations/0178_payments_reconcile_checkpoint.sql` adds `payments.reconcile_checkpoint` (one row: the start of the last run that finished; app role SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE of that column only); each run reads every charge created since the earlier of now − 7 days and that time − 1 day, with no cap (the charge list, `GET /v1/charges` with `created[gte]`, has no 30-day limit), so no charge is skipped however long the outage; when the gap since the last finished run is over 2 days it also raises one High `payments.reconcile_gap` alert, as information only (it skips nothing); the checkpoint moves only when a run finishes. (2) `ReconcileStripe::list_charges` (:63) returns an unbounded `Vec`; it becomes a paged read (`since`, a cursor, a page size of at most 100) and the run handles one page at a time in bounded batches, committing page by page, so memory and transaction size do not grow with volume; the FEE-030 cent-match totals (gross charges, refunds, disputes, fees) accumulate across pages and are compared once at the end of the run. (3) `own_refund` (:357) records a refund at the charged amount; it uses T333's check: a reported amount that differs or a currency other than `usd` records Stripe's amount and raises the same High alert. Tests in `tests/integration/tests/reconcile_catch_up.rs` (TD-FEE-60) with the fake `ReconcileStripe`: a 10-day outage reads back to the checkpoint less a day; a 40-day one reads every charge back to its checkpoint and raises the information alert once; the cent match over several pages equals the match over one; 250 charges are read in three pages; a partial refund found by the reconcile alerts; a failed run leaves the checkpoint. tasks.goal: Sixth audit U-06 (D-2307; TXT-012, TXT-020, CON-008, CON-018; D-801): a text stopped by a non-database module error (`Halt::Failed`) is answered 200 and, after T325, raises an alert, but nothing processes it again; D-2284's reason (no body to replay) was incomplete: Twilio keeps the body until the app redacts it on day 31 (`app/messaging/src/purge.rs:3`) and the inbox row holds the MessageSid. After T325: (1) `app/server/src/inbound_text.rs`: a `Halt::Failed` text also queues one `messaging.inbound_retry` task in the delivery's transaction (payload the inbox row ID only; dedupe per inbox row), retried at most 3 times with backoff (5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours); the last failure leaves T325's alert open and adds nothing. (2) `app/adapters/src/sms.rs`: `SmsBodyRead::fetch_message_body(sid)` (GET Messages/{sid}.json) answers the body, or `Gone` for a redacted or unknown message; `stand_ins/twilio.py` already serves that GET (D-2156) and gains only what the contract test needs. (3) `app/server/src/inbound_retry.rs` (registered in the shared `app/server/src/bin/worker.rs` under the Twilio settings): it reads the inbox row, fetches the body, runs it through the same scrubbing reader (`privacy::api::read_inbound_for`) and then the same steps in the same order as the route, skipping the inbox insert; it never stores or logs the body (D-801). Three rules: (a) opt-out and HELP always run (CON-008, CON-018); (b) if a newer inbox row from the same sender has already been processed, the retry does only (a) and closes, so stale content never overrides what she said since, and T325's alert stays as the record; (c) anything the retry sends goes through the normal outbound path under quiet hours (8 a.m. to 8 p.m. in the stricter of Arizona and the area code's time, QH-001), never as an immediate reply outside them. Before building, read how a `Halt::Failed` delivery commits the steps that ran before the failure and state it: each step is either keyed once per inbox row or MessageSid, so a repeat changes nothing, or the retry starts after the last committed step; a step that cannot be made safe to repeat stops this task, and it is reported instead. `Gone` (redacted on day 31, or by `Delete my data`) closes the task with no error. Permanent classes are not retried: a delivery refused as `BadWebhook`, a sender on the suppression list, and a step that answered a known refusal (`Halt::Ends`). tasks.title: portals and server: security-event rows are capped per address, webhook refusals are security events, and expired sessions are swept
tasks.goal: Fourth external audit F14, F5 and F7 (D-2207; SEC-048, SEC-016, SEC-004): (1) `portals::security`'s refusal (`app/portals/src/security.rs:96`) takes a pool connection and writes a security-event row before any limit, so a flood of cross-site or bad-CSRF requests turns each into a database write. An in-process counter, checked before the pool is touched, writes at most N rows per (event kind, client address as SEC-040 takes it, route) per minute and only counts the rest, logged as one line per minute with the count and no address; the 403 answer is unchanged. N is a setting in the shared `app/core/src/settings.rs` whose default is `EVENTS_PER_HOUR_ALERT` (50, `app/portals/src/security.rs:59`) and which is clamped up to it (a lower value is raised to it and logged at start-up), because the burst alert counts stored rows over the last hour (`security.rs:318`), so a cap below the threshold would stop it from ever firing. Until T135 proves that the edge overwrites the client-address header, a forged header must not buy a fresh cap: the counter also keeps a per-(kind, route) ceiling of N rows per minute across all addresses, so a flood with a new forged address on each request still writes at most N rows a minute per kind and route (the burst alert fires from those). (2) The Stripe, Twilio text and Twilio voice webhook routes answer a source or signature refusal 403 with a log line and record no security event, so SEC-048's hourly alert never sees them and a rotated Stripe address list fails silently. `app/server/src/webhook_refusals.rs` is a layer the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs` puts on those three routers only: each 403 they answer records one `webhook_signature_failed` event (route and request ID, no actor) through `portals::api::record_security_event`, under the same cap; first check that those routes answer 403 for nothing else, and if one does, tell the cases apart without reading the body. (3) Expired sessions are never removed (`app/portals/src/session.rs:165` deletes only a replaced cookie's row): a daily `portals.session_sweep` task, registered in the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs` and queued once a day like the purge sweep, deletes `portals.session` rows expired more than a day earlier, in batches. (4) Sixth audit U-08 (D-2306; SEC-014, SEC-040): `core.rate_limit` rows are never deleted (`prune`, `app/core/src/rate_limit.rs:230`, has no production caller) and their bucket names hold client addresses. A daily `core.rate_limit_prune` task, registered in the shared `app/server/src/lib.rs` and seeded in `worker.rs`'s `schedule_start` under a per-day dedupe key, deletes rows whose window started more than the longest configured window plus one day ago, in batches of at most 5,000 rows each in its own short statement (`prune_batch`, added to `rate_limit.rs`); it is registered, not deferred, in T327's registry. No index is added: once pruned daily the table holds a few days of windows. Tests in `tests/security/tests/security_event_cap.rs` (TD-SEC-53) and `tests/integration/tests/session_sweep.rs` (TD-SEC-54, TD-SEC-58); every existing security-event and session test passes unchanged. Update the `portals` and `server` `CLAUDE.md` files and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: privacy and quotes: spaced gate codes, lower-case street addresses, spoken dashes, "it's Steve" names and (at)/(dot) emails are cut by the scrubber and the CARD-008 gate
tasks.goal: Nov 10 code review, privacy F1 (D-2622; AI-002, AI-020, CARD-007, CARD-008, PRIV-005, D-800): the scrubber (`privacy::api::scrub`) and the card's final gate (`quotes::api::final_gate`, `app/quotes/src/gate.rs:48`) both let these fake shapes through to the AI and to every business's job card before any pick: "Gate code is 4 4 1 2" and "Gate code 44 12" (`mark_codes`, `app/privacy/src/scrub.rs:640`, cuts only one token of 3 or more digits); "i live at 2150 mesquite in havasu" (`mark_bare_houses` needs a capitalised street, `titled`, `:624`); "928 dash 555 dash 0134" (`digit_form` breaks on "dash"); "Steve Smith here", "Hi, it is Steve", "Hey its steve" (`TRIGGERS`, `:197`, lacks "it is", "its", "call me" and "<name> here" at the start); "Sink is leaking. Best, Steve" and "Thanks, Steve Smith 928-555-0134" (`sign_off`, `:693`, lacks "best" and "cheers" and needs the name to be the last one or two tokens); "steve(at)gmail(dot)com" and "steve @ gmail.com" (one token with no `@`; the local part kept). Fix each root cause in `scrub.rs`: after a code cue, cut every following digit-form token within a few words while the run holds 3 or more digits; after "at", "live", "address" or "is", a 3- to 6-digit house number followed by a lower-case word that is not common is an address; "dash", "guion" and "space" join a spoken digit run; the new triggers and sign-offs, the name allowed before trailing contact tokens; `(at)`, `[at]`, `(dot)`, `[dot]` inside a token read as `@` and `.` before the email check, and a spaced `@` cuts both sides. In `gate.rs`, CARD-008 also cuts the rest of a sentence holding a code cue followed by digits. T350's rule holds for every new trigger: no opt-out, HELP or START word is taken as a name. Tests: every shape above joins `CONTACTS` in `app/privacy/src/tests/scrub.rs` (the 99% recall corpus; the bar is never lowered, every existing case and the precision cases stay unchanged), and `tests/integration/tests/scrub_contact_shapes.rs` (TD-AI-27) runs each through `scrub` with an empty context and then `final_gate` and asserts no digit run of the code, house number, phone, email local part or name is left, plus false-positive guards ("the 2 4x4 posts", "call me back", "it is leaking", "best price", "Ask for 3 quotes"); each shape fails on today's `main`. tasks.title: payments (harness): a successful charge writes its charge ledger entry with the Stripe charge ID, stores that ID in its evidence record and queues its receipt
tasks.goal: Nov 10 code review, payments F1, F3 and F5 (D-2623; FEE-013, FEE-028, FEE-030, FEE-031, FEE-042; D-1414, D-1557, D-1561): a successful charge writes its attempt status and `payments.charge_evidence` (`write_evidence`, `app/payments/src/charge.rs:656`, from `effects`, `app/payments/src/handlers.rs:144`) but no `charge` ledger entry: `record_fee_at_confirm` (`app/payments/src/service.rs:401`) has no caller and needs a `ch_` ID that nothing on the success path has (the adapter's `PaymentIntent`, `app/adapters/src/payments.rs:32`, has no `latest_charge`). So (1) a second job of the same customer is charged again, since `free_wins::is_repeat` reads only ledger rows (FEE-013); (2) the business statement and money view show no charges but do show their refunds (FEE-030); (3) once T328 schedules the reconcile, every legitimate charge raises a High `payments.unknown_charge` alert; (4) the evidence record lacks the charge ID (FEE-042); and (5) `queue_receipt` (`app/payments/src/receipts.rs:56`) has no caller, so no Ask Hava receipt is ever emailed (FEE-031; D-1557 and D-1561 named `write_evidence` as the caller and a task that never took it). Fix: the adapter's `PaymentIntent` gains `latest_charge: Option<String>` (`#[serde(default)]`) and the stand-in returns a `ch_` ID on a succeeded intent; the release proof's fresh fetch (`paid_release`, `app/payments/src/release_proof.rs:193`) requires a `ch_` `latest_charge` on a succeeded intent (a missing one is refused like any other unreadable field, so Stripe's resend retries it) and carries it to the success write; in the transaction that writes the evidence (`migrations/0180_payments_charge_id.sql` adds a nullable `stripe_charge_id` to `payments.charge_evidence`, append-only for the app role as before), the success path stores the charge ID, appends one `charge` ledger entry at the pick's stored fee (`payments.pick_fee`, equal to the checked intent amount) with that ID under the key `record_fee_at_confirm` derives (`CONFIRM_FEE_ACTION`, job and business), so the nightly reconcile converges on it instead of adding a second (`app/payments/src/reconcile.rs:381`), and calls `queue_receipt` when the evidence row was newly written; a replayed success writes nothing more. This harness task adopts the done tests that build `PaymentIntent` by name (`charge_attempts.rs`, `fee_limit_race.rs`, `stripe_webhook_dispatch.rs`, `confirm_and_pay.rs`, `fee_fixed_at_pick.rs`, `app/server/tests/request_timeout.rs`, `release_recovery.rs`): each literal gains a fake `ch_` ID, and no assertion is removed or weakened. Tests in `tests/integration/tests/charge_ledger_entry.rs` (TD-FEE-64), each failing on today's `main`: a stand-in success webhook leaves exactly one `charge` row with the `ch_` ID and the stored cents, the evidence row holds the same ID, and one `payments.receipt` task is queued; the replayed webhook adds no row and no task; `business_statement` totals equal the charges; a later pick of the same business on another job of the same customer is waived as `Repeat`; a reconcile run over the paid pick raises no `unknown_charge` alert and appends nothing. Money: 95% branch floor; the overseer runs an independent money review of the hand-in. Update the `payments` and `adapters` `CLAUDE.md` files, `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: payments: a won dispute records the countering fee's return and the disputed amount's return, and the reconcile compares only disputes not won
tasks.goal: Nov 10 code review, payments F2 (D-2625; FEE-027 to FEE-030, FEE-050; D-1383, D-1753): `charge.dispute.closed` (`dispute_closed`, `app/payments/src/routes.rs:489`) only writes an audit row and a High alert; it never reads the event's `status` (`read_object` keeps only `/id`), and no code writes `EntryKind::CounteringFeeReturn` (`app/payments/src/ledger.rs:32`). So when Casey wins a $75 dispute whose evidence was submitted, the ledger keeps the `dispute` 9000 and the `countering-fee` 1500 as lost, `MoneyView::net()` understates by $90 for good, the business statement shows a dispute it won, and the reconcile cannot see it because `MoneyTotals::of_stripe` counts a dispute whatever its status. D-1383 left "how a won dispute's returned amount is recorded" to the dispute tasks, and none took it. Fix: `dispute_closed` reads `status`; on `won`, in the event's transaction and once per dispute, it appends a `countering-fee-return` equal to the recorded countering fee (when one was recorded, FEE-050) and a `dispute-reversal` of the disputed amount without Stripe's non-refundable dispute fee, the stored code made only by a `LedgerEntry` constructor and folded by every ledger reader as a negative dispute, as D-1753 did for `refund-reversal` (not an `EntryKind` variant, so `portals`' exhaustive statement match is untouched; `migrations/0181_payments_dispute_reversal.sql` adds the code to the ledger's `kind` check; FEE-028 lists it since D-2625); any other closing status changes nothing but the audit and alert as today. The reconcile compares the disputed amounts of disputes that are open or lost only, reading each dispute's status through T335's `DisputeStripe`. Tests in `tests/integration/tests/dispute_won.rs` (TD-FEE-65), each failing on today's `main`: after a submitted dispute, a `won` closure leaves `MoneyView.dispute_fees` equal to the non-refundable dispute fee only and the net disputed amount 0, and the business statement shows the dispute as won; the same event again appends nothing; a `lost` closure changes no ledger row; a won dispute with no countering fee appends no `countering-fee-return`; the reconcile over a won dispute raises no difference. Money: 95% branch floor; the overseer runs an independent money review of the hand-in. Update the `payments` `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: privacy: key rotation re-seals stored photos too, so dropping the old vault key never makes a photo unreadable
tasks.goal: Nov 10 code review, privacy F2 (D-2626; PRIV-023, PRIV-024): `rotate_batch` (`app/privacy/src/vault.rs:668`) moves `privacy.contact` and `privacy.stated_name` to the newest key, but no code re-seals `privacy.photo` (only the INSERT at `app/privacy/src/photos.rs:358`; the app role has no UPDATE on it), and `PhotoSeal::open` needs the row's `key_version` in its key map. The documented drill (`app/privacy/CLAUDE.md`: run `rotate_batch` until it returns 0, then drop `1:`) therefore makes every photo sealed under v1 fail with `PhotoError::Sealed` (not even `LinkDead`) for the rest of its life (job close plus 30 days, longer under a dispute hold), or forces the old key to stay live, which defeats a rotation after a key leak. Fix: `rotate_photos(db, seal, storage, limit)` in `photos.rs` re-seals, in bounded batches, each photo whose `key_version` is below the active one: it reads the object, opens it under its version and AAD, seals it under the active version and AAD, writes it as a new object, then moves the row to the new object and version in one statement and deletes the old object only after that commits (a crash at any step leaves a readable photo and at most one orphan, which the orphan sweep removes, D-1793); `migrations/0182_privacy_photo_reseal.sql` grants the app role UPDATE on exactly those columns of `privacy.photo`. The drill in the crate doc becomes: run `rotate_batch` and `rotate_photos` until both return 0, then drop the old key. No plaintext is logged or kept; open audits are not written for a re-seal (it returns nothing to a reader). Tests in `tests/integration/tests/photo_key_rotation.rs` (TD-PRIV-24), each failing on today's `main` where noted: a photo stored under v1, then the drill with `2:K2,1:K1`, then `VAULT_KEY=2:K2` alone: `open_link` still returns the same bytes (fails today); a run over no old photos returns 0; a re-seal interrupted after the new object is written leaves the photo readable under the old row; the row's version and the AAD bind the new object. `the_rotation_drill_moves_every_row_to_v2` passes unchanged. Update the `privacy` `CLAUDE.md`, the key-rotation runbook line it cites, and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: picks: the release claim re-checks the pick under its row lock, and a fraud end refuses a pick already released
tasks.goal: Nov 10 code review, privacy F3 (D-2627; PICK-022, PRIV-005, FEE-052): the release claim reads its target unlocked (`show`, `app/picks/src/release.rs:282`, through `release_target`) and `record` (`:394`) inserts `picks.release` with `ON CONFLICT (pick_id)` only, while `fraud_warning` (`app/picks/src/unreachable_refund.rs:490`) decides on the caller's `released` snapshot and `end_pick` (`:439`) checks only `status = paid`. When a payment success and T281's early-fraud-warning task run together for one pick, the warning can refund and end the pick as `fraud_refunded` while the release, which read it as confirmed and not ended, commits its row and opens the name and address: the business gets both the refund and the details (FEE-052 ends only an unreleased paid pick). Fix: `record` locks the pick (`SELECT … FROM picks.pick WHERE id = $1 AND status = $want AND ended_at IS NULL FOR UPDATE`) inside the claim's transaction and answers `MovedOn` when it is gone, before any vault read; `end_pick` and `fraud_warning` refuse a pick that has a `picks.release` row, read in the same statement (`AND NOT EXISTS …`), whatever the caller's snapshot says, so a released pick goes to Casey's decision list as FEE-052 says. Tests in `tests/integration/tests/release_fraud_race.rs` (TD-PICK-59), with two connections and a held row lock (no sleeps): a pick ended between `release_target` and `record` gives `MovedOn`, no release row and no `vault_read.picks.release` audit row (fails today); a fraud warning on a pick whose release committed first lists it for Casey and refunds nothing; the plain release and the plain fraud end behave as before. Update the `picks` `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: messaging and server: the worker sends queued texts, re-checking quiet hours, the line and the suppression list at the moment of sending
tasks.goal: Nov 10 code review, messaging F4, and D-2188's unowned follow-up (D-2628; QH-001, QH-006, QH-008, TXT-021, CON-009, CON-030): nothing in production sends a `messaging.outbox` row: `send_on_line` (`app/messaging/src/mode.rs:225`) and `send_checked` (`app/messaging/src/optout.rs:310`) have only test callers, so no consent text, HELP reply, opt-out confirmation or job text ever reaches a phone; and both check the suppression list and the line but never quiet hours, the outbox has no not-before time (only retries have `next_retry`), so once a sender drains rows as written, every row queued at night (a held missed-call text, a business auto reply) goes at once. D-2188 left two duties to "the owner of the outbox sender": a row queued while its line was paused must not go out late once texting is back. Fix: (1) `migrations/0183_messaging_outbox_not_before.sql` adds a nullable `not_before` to `messaging.outbox`, set at enqueue from the row's message kind and `rules::decide` (`Hold { until }` gives `until`), with no change to `NewText` or any struct done tests build by name; (2) `send_checked` re-runs the quiet-hours rule for the row's kind at the send instant (QH-001, and QH-008 for a retry) and refuses with a hold that sets `not_before` instead of reaching the carrier, so the rule no longer depends on each enqueuer; the CON-018 HELP reply and the CON-009 confirmation keep their any-hour rule; (3) `app/messaging/src/outbox_sender.rs`: a `messaging.send_due` worker task, registered in `app/server/src/bin/worker.rs` (shared) with the Twilio settings like `picks.line_retry`, claims due rows (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, `not_before` passed, not blocked) in bounded batches and sends each through `send_on_line`, outside any transaction across the carrier call; it re-queues itself; (4) a non-reply row queued while its line was paused, switched off or suspended is marked expired with one audit row and never sent (D-2188), and a CON-009 confirmation older than 5 minutes is never sent (CON-030 forbids a later confirmation). Every enqueuer keeps its own behaviour; `suspension_mode.rs` and every TD-TXT and TD-CON case pass unchanged. Tests in `tests/integration/tests/outbox_sender.rs` (TD-QH-05), through the worker with the stand-in Twilio: a `caller_missed` row queued at 21:30 Arizona time for a 928 number is not sent at 21:31 and is sent at 08:00; a consent text queued at 14:00 is sent at once; a suppressed number gets nothing but HELP; a row queued while the line was suspended is expired, not sent, when the line reopens; a confirmation is sent within 5 minutes or never; two workers send a row once. Update the `messaging` and `server` `CLAUDE.md` files, `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: server, messaging and intake: START into an open request restarts with the consent text, an opt-out while texting is off is confirmed by email, CANCEL pauses the job, and a listed homeowner who writes is emailed or listed for Casey
tasks.goal: Nov 10 code review, messaging F2, F3 and F5 and CON-016 (D-2629; CON-001, CON-015, CON-016, CON-028, CON-029, CON-030; D-1229). After T336 (the last earlier owner of `inbound_text.rs`): (1) START into a still-open request: the route treats `Outcome::Resubscribed` like `Open` (`app/server/src/inbound_text.rs:387`) and passes "START" to `intake::receive_reply`, whose rules send no consent text once one was sent (`app/intake/src/rules.rs:100`), so a homeowner who opted out and texts START a day later gets no consent text and "START" is heard as an answer (CON-015, CON-001). Now the route calls a new `intake::api::restart_after_start` (`app/intake/src/resubscribe.rs`), which queues the consent text again under the START inbox row as its subject, records it as sent, and passes nothing to the open question. (2) An opt-out while the homeowner line is switched off, suspended or restored and waiting gets no confirmation: `confirm` (`app/messaging/src/optout.rs:195`) answers "email instead" only for the ops pause and never reads `messaging.mode_state`, and the route drops the `email` flag (`inbound_text.rs:372`). Now `confirm` decides "paused" from the same facts `send_on_line` uses, queues no text then, and `app/messaging/src/optout_email.rs` queues the CON-030 email confirmation through the email outbox when an email is on file (vault lookup, never logged). (3) D-1229 named the inbound route to call `intake::api::on_opt_out` after `Outcome::OptedOut`; no task did (T330 builds only the handler of the event it queues), so a sole CANCEL while a pick waits for Confirm neither pauses the job nor withdraws the pick, and the business can still pay and get her details: the route now calls it in the delivery's transaction. (4) CON-016: a listed homeowner who writes without START (`Outcome::Suppressed`) is emailed once a day at most when an email is on file ("You opted out of texts…", English and Spanish email templates, the copy panel's drafts), and otherwise recorded as one `messaging.optout_wrote_again` row (IDs only) that T204's weekly digest counts; the CON-017 emergency alert is unchanged. Tests in `tests/integration/tests/optout_followups.rs` (TD-CON-33) through the served route, each failing on today's `main`: open request, STOP, then START with `OptOutType=START` gives one `consent` outbox row for the START inbox row and no intake answer holding "START"; a suspended line, a phrase opt-out and an email on file give one email confirmation and no outbox text row; CANCEL with a waiting pick gives an `intake.homeowner_pause` row and the queued `intake.opted_out_live_job` event; a listed homeowner's plain text gives one email (with email) or one digest row (without). Every TD-TXT, TD-CON and TD-SEC-52 case passes unchanged. Update the `server`, `messaging` and `intake` `CLAUDE.md` files and `docs/decisions.md`.

tasks.title: messaging: the Canadian area codes for the HELP roaming line come from the quiet-hours table, which gains the four new Ontario codes
tasks.goal: Nov 10 code review, messaging F6 (D-2630; CON-018, QH-002, D-100): the two area-code tables disagree. `CANADIAN_AREA_CODES` (`app/messaging/src/keywords.rs:25`) lists 382, 683, 753 and 942, which `app/messaging/area_codes.json` (the quiet-hours zone table) lacks, so a homeowner on one of those numbers gets the HELP reply and nothing else (`NotTextable`); and 257 (British Columbia) is in the zone table but not in the Canadian list, so its HELP reply misses the roaming line. Fix: the four Ontario codes join `area_codes.json` under their zone (each checked against the North American numbering plan's published assignment, cited in the decision), and the Canadian set is derived from the zone table's Canadian entries (one source; a code's country is read from its zone or a tag in the same file), so the two cannot drift. Tests in `app/messaging/src/tests/area_codes.rs` (TD-QH-06), each failing on today's `main`: every code of the Canadian set has a zone in the table; 257 gets the roaming line; 382, 683, 753 and 942 are textable inside 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. in both Arizona and Toronto time; a US code never gets the roaming line. Every TD-QH and TD-CON case passes unchanged. Update the `messaging` `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/decisions.md`.
